units.translation: || On the disyllabic form γαῖα [earth], which the poets use where the meter demands it, has been discussed in its proper place.
and all-mother earth.
the farthest place of the earth.
and inhabitants of the Colchian land.
the mighty strength of earth and the heavenly pole,
the depths of the earth rumble below.
What land? What race?
where on earth have I, wretched, wandered?
on the farthest borders of the earth.
I am driven from land to land.
you will come to a far-off land.
and the sea-born trident, shaker of the earth, a plague.
to my children and to the earth, my mother, dearest nurse.
and the free land and city of Cadmus.
What will you do, ancient Ares, to your own land?
guardians of this land's towers.
a confused gift of earth.
Would that the gods might destroy these men in the land.
to the visitors of the land.
he calls upon the ancestral gods of his fatherland.
with the dear ruins of the earth.
queen of this land.
he is gone to the land of the Ionians.
it is necessary to pour libations to the earth and to the dead.
I will come bringing gifts to the earth and to the dead.
O cities of all the Asian land.
from the land of Asia.
a settler in a harsh land.
the ground of the Achaean land.
throughout the Asian land.
falling to the ground.
to all this land of yours.
For the earth itself is their ally.
having come to the land of Hellas.
near the land of Plataea.
seated upon this land.
and the land laments its native youth.
and to the fatherland.
the gods of the captured land.
the tombs of the Trojan land.
love for this fatherland.
Do you say that the army longs for this land?
the dear power of this land.
land appearing to sailors beyond hope.
but blood once fallen to the ground.
a stranger to this land.
from this land.
O earth, earth, would that you had received me.
from above the earth.
ruler of this land.
For I have come to this land.
with the gods and the land and victorious justice.
For the offerings from the earth to the hostile dead.
the tomb of a land across the sea.
I pray to this land and to my father's tomb.
for the earth nourishes many things.
a stranger to this land.
the navel of the earth.
both himself and the land.
until he goes beneath the earth.
wasting away upon the earth they diminish.
destroying the land from Scamander.
a guard of the land:
deprived of his fatherland.
in this land.
to this land.
to dwell beneath the earth.
you will fall in love with this land.
both land and city.
kindly-minded, come here to the land.
whose city, whose land and white water.
from the land of Aeria.
founders of this land (or founder).
therefore he drove him from the land.
the name of the greatest land.
inhabitants from this land.
who were then lawful inhabitants of the land.
to dwell as a settler in this land.
the ground of the earth.
tributes of the land.
may Zeus bring the land to fulfillment with all-season fruit.
and the gods who hold the land.
to bring to the land.
O earth, mound.
and in the land.
he howls before the land.
the inhabitants of this land.
of the Ethiopian land.
Zeus is the sky, Zeus is the earth.
a bridge yoking two lands.
for from heaven and from earth.
and in the land.
beneath the earth and below in Hades.
and beneath the body of the earth there will be boundless wealth.
to send good things to you and to your child from beneath the earth to the light.
to the gods and to the dear ones beneath the earth.
chambers beneath the earth.
beneath the darkness of the earth.
those beneath the earth.
